text: Preview can surface three genuinely different kinds of problems, and they don't all mean the same thing or get fixed the same way: collisions, missing dependencies, and skipped records.

A collision happens when the version of something inside the Update Set differs from the version currently sitting on the target instance. This is almost always caused by someone editing that same thing -- the same Business Rule, the same ACL -- directly on the target, outside this Update Set entirely. The more admins actively customizing an instance, the more often Preview will surface one.

A missing dependency happens when the Update Set references something, commonly a Script Include a Business Rule calls, or a table a new field depends on, that doesn't exist yet on the target instance, because that referenced piece actually lives in a different Update Set that hasn't been applied yet. Commit the dependent change first, and the target ends up with a rule calling something that, from its point of view, simply isn't there.

A skipped record is different from the first two -- it isn't something ServiceNow detects automatically. It means an administrator, during Preview, deliberately chose not to apply one specific flagged change, usually because they judged it unsafe or unnecessary on that particular target. A skip that's later forgotten can leave an instance assuming something was applied that actually wasn't.

The fix for a collision: review both versions side by side, what's in the Update Set versus what's currently on the target, and deliberately choose which one to keep, rather than letting either side win by default. For missing dependencies, the fix is almost entirely prevention: apply Update Sets to the target in the correct dependency order, so whatever defines the Script Include or table is committed before the Update Set that references it.

For skipped records, the fix is documentation and follow-through: note what was skipped and why, and revisit it deliberately rather than letting it quietly fall through the cracks across future promotions. Next up: a full worked lab walking through building an Update Set, moving it to Test, and resolving a real collision there.
